figures.caption: Table 1: More streams give more accuracy, and less credit to the brain. Within-listener, MATCHED, chance 0.25. The four fused models share streams, data, folds, architecture and listener adaptation; they differ only in the contribution hinge and in modality dropout. ϕm is each stream’s Shapley credit and the five add up to the contribution. The EEG-only model shows how much credit the brain earns on its own. Appendix J gives the same four models on unseen listeners.
Table 3: Audio-only acceptance probe: what a linear reader takes from the candidates alone, with no access to any recording. A shortcut-free construction must sit at chance.

Figure 2: Shapley credit per stream, stacked, for the four fused rows of Table 1. Each bar’s total height is that model’s contribution v(M) − v(∅), decomposed exactly. The question the figure answers is not how tall the bars are but how much of each one is blue.

Table 7: What the full battery says about two public datasets. Accuracy and contribution for the unconstrained coupling branch, then contribution with the branch confined to the causal (+125 · · · + 1109ms) and mirrored acausal (−1109 · · · − 125ms) lag bands. Folds+ is for the unconstrained branch. The last row is MAESTRO’s same-talker K = 2 result, the reference for what a directional response looks like.

Table 8: Two-talker accuracy at 5 s: with each paper’s own split, and without leakage. The first five rows decode the direction of attention from EEG alone, and are NeuroToken’s re-runs on KU Leuven listeners 1–4 (Alavi & Williamson, 2026); the headline numbers in those papers are higher still, 95–97% at 1 s. NeuroToken and MERIT decode the attended talker from EEG and the candidate speech. NeuroToken holds out whole trials; MERIT holds out whole stimuli and uses matched candidates. “Unseen” means listeners not seen in training.

Figure 3: Contribution against decision-window length, within-listener, MATCHED. Left: contribution for the four stream sets measured at every window; the eleven stream sets at 2 and 5 s are in Table 13. Right: the full model’s shuffled accuracy, which is what the contribution subtracts, and the linear audio probe, both measured at each window. The model’s shuffled accuracy stays within 0.015 of chance throughout; the probe varies more, between 0.23 and 0.30.

Table 12: Orienting-free decoding and neural directionality. EEG only unless stated, withinsubject, W = 10 s. Same-talker candidates are the attended talker at different times, so slot index carries no spatial meaning and no orienting cue can help. The lag band is set by the encoder’s direction plus an eight-sample shift; a contribution as large in the acausal band would indicate a shared artifact rather than envelope tracking.

Table 13: Every stream set at the two shortest decision windows, within-subject (content-disjoint, five folds), MATCHED, K = 4, chance 0.25, hop = W/2. Contribution is accuracy minus the model’s own permutation null; p is the permutation p-value, floored at 0.048 for twenty permutations. The first block is single streams, the second EEG paired with each behavioural stream.

Table 14: Hinge, selection rule and modality dropout at W = 10 s, per-window decisions — the earlier operating point, kept because it varies the selection rule, which Table 1 does not. Identical streams, data and folds; within-subject, MATCHED, W = 10 s, chance 0.25. ϕm is Shapley credit and sums to the contribution by construction. The single-stream EEG model is shown for reference.
